creator: Alexander Terp
description:
I wanted a skill whose SKILL.md comes from a CLI: `<tool> skill` prints the skill text to stdout. The natural shape is a skill dir whose tai.yaml has a command include writing `$TAI_DEST_DIR/SKILL.md`, but no `dest` works:

- A dest that resolves to the skill root is rejected (`internal/install/command_include.go:46`): `dest "<dest>" resolves to the skill root; choose a subdirectory (e.g. refs/)`.
- A file dest (`SKILL.md`) would become a directory, since the staging dir is swapped into `dest` whole.

The tai skill's Command Includes section doesn't say command includes are directory-only, so I wrote a README example that could not work before finding the check. The workaround is a `type: command` source that writes `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, declared separately in each config repo that installs the skill.

Suggested, either:

- Allow a command include to produce SKILL.md: swap single files, or merge the staging dir into the skill root instead of replacing `dest`.
- Or document it: say in the Command Includes section that dest must be a subdirectory, and point at command sources for a generated SKILL.md.

(Moved from GitHub issue #11.)
title: A command include cannot write a skill's root SKILL.md
